scenarios.name: Artifact mismatch: Intent A combined with Confirmation B
scenarios.threat: An attacker swaps a confirmation from one booking onto another to hijack terms or price.
scenarios.protects: Every approval confirmation is cryptographically bound to its exact hold ID.

scenarios.name: Confirmation token reuse with altered idempotency key
scenarios.threat: An attacker replays a spent buyer approval using a fresh idempotency key.
scenarios.protects: Confirmations are one-time records locked and stamped consumed in PostgreSQL.

scenarios.name: One hundred simultaneous commits with one confirmation
scenarios.threat: A burst of parallel commit requests tries to book or charge a single approval twice.
scenarios.protects: PostgreSQL row locks and GiST constraints ensure at most one winner succeeds.

scenarios.name: Actor, OAuth client, and tenant substitution prevention
scenarios.threat: A caller takes a valid booking intent and submits it under a different tenant, app, or user.
scenarios.protects: Commit verifies signed tenant, client, and user claims against the authenticated session.

scenarios.name: Transport surface substitution: intent replayed through unlisted transport
scenarios.threat: An agent tries to replay a web-only booking intent over the external MCP channel.
scenarios.protects: Each signed intent pins its permitted transport surfaces in its verified claims.

scenarios.name: Tool/schema/version substitution after prepare
scenarios.threat: A client alters tool schema or version between holding a slot and committing it.
scenarios.protects: Hold snapshots lock the original schema hash and policy terms at prepare time.

scenarios.name: Duplicate JSON keys rejected before object parsing
scenarios.threat: An attacker sends duplicate JSON keys hoping the validator and handler disagree on price.
scenarios.protects: The Fastify parser inspects raw JSON bytes and rejects duplicate keys with HTTP 400.

scenarios.name: Unicode NFC/NFD canonicalization differences
scenarios.threat: Crafted decomposed Unicode strings attempt to bypass signature or idempotency checks.
scenarios.protects: Strings undergo deterministic NFC normalization and RFC 8785 canonicalization before hashing.

scenarios.name: Money validation: exponent notation, excessive precision, negative and overflow
scenarios.threat: Malformed numbers like 1e5 or oversized integers try to corrupt payment math.
scenarios.protects: All money values use validated integer minor-unit strings with 64-bit bounds checks.

scenarios.name: Zero-decimal and three-decimal currency scale mismatch
scenarios.threat: Assumed 2-decimal math overcharges or undercharges zero-decimal and 3-decimal currencies.
scenarios.protects: Currency scaling uses an explicit ISO-4217 table matched against the service snapshot.

scenarios.name: Commit at exp - 1, exactly exp, and after exp
scenarios.threat: Stale signed intents or holds are submitted at or past their expiration boundary.
scenarios.protects: Expiry checks enforce strict less-than inequalities on signed tokens and DB clock time.

scenarios.name: JWS attack suite: alg none, algorithm confusion, unknown kid, remote jku, wrong typ
scenarios.threat: Attackers forge booking intents using alg:none, foreign keys (jku), unknown key IDs, or wrong token types.
scenarios.protects: JWS verification requires ES256, velvetai-intent+jwt type, local trusted keys, and no remote URLs.

scenarios.name: Approval URL shared with another buyer
scenarios.threat: Knowing someone else's approval URL lets another signed-in user approve their booking.
scenarios.protects: Approval rejects any authenticated user whose ID and email do not match the hold owner.

scenarios.name: Role or tenant membership revoked after approval
scenarios.threat: An attacker keeps acting with an old token after their tenant access was revoked.
scenarios.protects: Local PostgreSQL memberships and role versions are checked on every protected request.

scenarios.name: MCP action: accept without browser approval completion
scenarios.threat: An MCP client sends accepted flags claiming the human approved without completing browser approval.
scenarios.protects: Server commits require an opaque hashed confirmation minted exclusively on the approval endpoint.

scenarios.name: Transaction crash boundary: crash after confirmation consumption
scenarios.threat: A process crash mid-commit leaves the buyer confirmation spent while the booking stays uncommitted.
scenarios.protects: Confirmation consumption, booking state change, and outbox insert share one atomic DB transaction.

scenarios.name: Transaction crash boundary: crash after outbox insertion
scenarios.threat: A crash right after saving a booking leaves side effects stuck or lost.
scenarios.protects: Outbox events commit in the same DB transaction and recover cleanly via leased worker polling.

scenarios.name: PayPal capture succeeds before local persistence
scenarios.threat: Network loss right after PayPal captures funds leaves the booking status unknown locally.
scenarios.protects: PayPal orders embed tenant and booking references so reconciliation and webhooks heal state safely.

scenarios.name: Cancellation/expiry/commit race prevention
scenarios.threat: Simultaneous expiry, cancellation, or commit corrupts claim blocking state or double-books a slot.
scenarios.protects: Row-level locks, optimistic booking versioning, and DB check constraints forbid invalid claim drift.

scenarios.name: Long-transaction expiry uses database clock_timestamp()
scenarios.threat: A long-running database transaction exploits snapshot start time to commit an expired hold.
scenarios.protects: Hold expiry checks evaluate PostgreSQL clock_timestamp() in real wall-clock time.

scenarios.name: RLS context leak through a one-connection pool
scenarios.threat: Pooled database connections leak Tenant A's tenant setting into Tenant B's query.
scenarios.protects: FORCE RLS binds queries to transaction-local app.tenant_id under non-bypass runtime role.

scenarios.name: Outbox relay resumes after its lease was reassigned
scenarios.threat: A paused worker wakes up late and acknowledges an outbox job already claimed by another worker.
scenarios.protects: Outbox acknowledgments fence updates on the exact UUID lease token.

scenarios.name: BullMQ worker executes a stalled job twice
scenarios.threat: At-least-once background job redelivery triggers duplicate captures or duplicate notifications.
scenarios.protects: Workers verify terminal DB states and deterministic request keys before executing side effects.

scenarios.name: PayPal simulator event sent to production webhook route
scenarios.threat: Unverified or mismatched environment webhooks try to mark unpaid bookings as confirmed.
scenarios.protects: Webhook verification requires cryptographic PayPal signature check and matching environment/connection.

scenarios.name: Refund performed externally in PayPal dashboard
scenarios.threat: A refund issued outside velvetAI leaves the local ledger and booking state out of sync.
scenarios.protects: Verified PAYMENT.CAPTURE.REFUNDED webhooks reconcile captures and post reversal entries.

scenarios.name: Webhook certificate URL validation (SSRF / non-PayPal host prevention)
scenarios.threat: Forged webhook headers point cert_url at internal cloud metadata IPs or attacker servers.
scenarios.protects: Certificate URLs must strictly use HTTPS on official api[.sandbox].paypal.com hosts.

scenarios.name: Order reports COMPLETED while capture reports PENDING
scenarios.threat: Trusting an order status alone confirms an appointment before PayPal capture finishes settling.
scenarios.protects: Bookings transition to CONFIRMED strictly when the underlying capture status equals COMPLETED.

scenarios.name: Wrong sandbox app or wrong environment webhook
scenarios.threat: Webhooks from another sandbox app or environment try to forge payment events for this tenant.
scenarios.protects: Every webhook validates against the tenant connection's configured PayPal webhook ID.

scenarios.name: MCP protocol header/body mismatch
scenarios.threat: A client sends mismatched header and body protocol versions to confuse version guards.
scenarios.protects: The stateless MCP endpoint requires exact header and metadata version agreement.

scenarios.name: Missing protocol version header on stateless MCP endpoint
scenarios.threat: An unversioned client omits the MCP-Protocol-Version header to bypass strict parsing.
scenarios.protects: All POST /mcp requests without MCP-Protocol-Version fail closed with HTTP 400.

scenarios.name: Unsupported protocol revision rejection
scenarios.threat: An attacker downgrades MCP to an older legacy revision with weaker session rules.
scenarios.protects: POST /mcp rejects legacy revisions like 2024-11-05 at the transport gate with HTTP 400.

scenarios.name: GET/DELETE session request against stateless MCP endpoint
scenarios.threat: A caller probes stateful SSE or session termination endpoints on GET or DELETE /mcp.
scenarios.protects: Only stateless POST /mcp is allowed; GET and DELETE return 405 Method Not Allowed.

scenarios.name: Forged Auth0 issuer in bearer token
scenarios.threat: An attacker mints JWTs from an untrusted third-party identity provider.
scenarios.protects: RS256 JWKS verification enforces an exact match on the configured Auth0 issuer.

scenarios.name: Wrong Auth0 audience or resource claim
scenarios.threat: A valid JWT issued for a different API or service is replayed against velvetAI.
scenarios.protects: Bearer tokens must explicitly match the target REST or MCP audience identifier.

scenarios.name: Missing required scope guard enforcement
scenarios.threat: A read-only token tries to invoke write operations like preparing a hold or judge reset.
scenarios.protects: Every protected route and tool validates required scopes before executing logic.

scenarios.name: Revoked local PostgreSQL membership with valid Auth0 token
scenarios.threat: A kicked-out user continues calling endpoints until their JWT naturally expires.
scenarios.protects: Local PostgreSQL membership revocation and role_version take effect immediately.

scenarios.name: Execution of unallowlisted tool
scenarios.threat: An agent or model tries to call an arbitrary or undocumented tool name.
scenarios.protects: Only explicitly registered and schema-validated tools exist in sharedToolRegistry.

scenarios.name: Model attempts commit without verified browser confirmation
scenarios.threat: An AI assistant tries to autonomously commit a booking or capture customer funds.
scenarios.protects: Commit tools are blocked for model execution with COMMIT_NOT_PERMITTED_FOR_AI.

scenarios.name: MCP navigation accepted but approval not completed in browser
scenarios.threat: Visiting or fetching the approval page link is treated as consent without clicking Approve.
scenarios.protects: Only a POST /confirm by the signed-in buyer marks a confirmation eligible for commit.

scenarios.name: WebMCP cross-origin frame attempts execution
scenarios.threat: An embedded third-party iframe tries to invoke velvetAI browser WebMCP tools.
scenarios.protects: Same-origin Permissions-Policy headers restrict tool exposure strictly to self.

scenarios.name: WebMCP consequential hint removed by malicious client
scenarios.threat: A browser extension strips advisory tool risk hints expecting the server to skip checks.
scenarios.protects: Advisory hints never weaken backend confirmation, auth, or payment invariants.

scenarios.name: Tool/schema version changed after prepare
scenarios.threat: A caller tampers with schema versions mid-flight between prepare and commit.
scenarios.protects: Commit validates the signed intent schema bindings before finalizing state.

scenarios.name: Prompt injection in user chat input
scenarios.threat: A user embeds fake <system> tags inside chat trying to override concierge rules.
scenarios.protects: Role tags are stripped and user text is fenced inside untrusted input delimiters.

scenarios.name: Prompt injection in third-party tool output
scenarios.threat: Malicious customer notes or service descriptions instruct the AI to auto-approve or pay.
scenarios.protects: Customer notes are stripped from model context and commits require browser confirmation.

scenarios.name: Tool-call loop exceeds maximum budget (20 calls)
scenarios.threat: A runaway or adversarial prompt traps Ask AI in an endless tool-calling loop.
scenarios.protects: Ask AI hard-caps tool invocations per turn at 20 calls and aborts overflow.

scenarios.name: Gemini provider timeout after 30-second budget
scenarios.threat: A stalled upstream AI provider hangs API worker threads and exhausts request capacity.
scenarios.protects: Every AI invocation enforces a 30-second AbortController timeout and concurrency cap.

scenarios.name: Fake model versus real-provider result labeling
scenarios.threat: Simulated offline AI responses could be misrepresented as live LLM verification.
scenarios.protects: AI status explicitly separates offline deterministic mode from verified Gemini calls.

scenarios.name: Confirmation token or OAuth token requested through model
scenarios.threat: Prompt injection asks the LLM to print confirmation tokens or Bearer secrets.
scenarios.protects: Raw confirmation and auth tokens never enter tool payloads or LLM message history.

scenarios.name: Agent approves its own hold with its M2M token
scenarios.threat: An autonomous MCP agent prepares a hold and tries to self-approve using its M2M token.
scenarios.protects: Approval rejects @clients M2M credentials with HTTP 403 HUMAN_APPROVAL_REQUIRED.

scenarios.name: Unauthenticated request confirms locator
scenarios.threat: An anonymous caller who guesses or sees an approval URL tries to confirm the hold.
scenarios.protects: Unauthenticated confirm requests fail closed with HTTP 401 and mint no confirmation.

scenarios.name: Buyer B confirms Buyer A's locator
scenarios.threat: A different signed-in user tries to approve and claim another customer's hold URL.
scenarios.protects: Approval verifies buyer identity against the hold owner and rejects mismatches with BUYER_MISMATCH.
